source: a true 3D room-decorating game (not a 2D, top-down, or UI/screen-based game): the player stands in a 3D room in third person and furnishes it by picking real furniture and props (such as a sofa, table, chair, lamp, plant, or rug) from an in-game catalog/menu and placing them into the room. Each furniture item must be a recognizable, real 3D furniture MODEL sourced from the Roblox asset library / Toolbox (search for the asset and insert the model), not a plain recolored box or a 2D image. Include a goal such as filling a set of placement slots or reaching a completion meter, and make sure placed items rest on the floor. The room and furniture must exist as 3D world objects with depth, not as a 2D/GUI layout. Do not ask any clarifying questions. Make any reasonable creative decisions yourself and build the complete, playable game now.

image_prompt.text: A catalog point in the room where furniture is chosen before being placed
Furniture stock drawn on from the catalog rather than gathered from the world
Designated floor placement slots around the room where furniture can be set down
a single furnishable room interior - floor, walls and open floor area with the player character standing in it in third person
real recognisable furniture models resting on the floor: sofa, table, chair, lamp, potted plant, rug

layout_placement.text: One placement slot volume per furniture position, tracked toward a completion meter
every placed item must rest on the floor plane rather than float

notes: Forced classification: this is a furnishing game, not a tycoon or an extraction sandbox. Simulations isolated plot was used because the room is the plot and the loop is placing objects in it; nothing in the index describes interior decorating.
No P3 despite the map being an interior: there is no exterior at all, so there is no outside-inside transition to generate.
collectible-nodes was kept per instruction but is wrong here - the catalog is a menu, not extractable ground.
The prompt forbids clarifying questions, so the open questions below are recorded rather than asked, and every gap was resolved by inference.

open_questions.ask: No style is stated beyond real furniture - should the room read as a contemporary apartment, a cosy cottage, or a bright stylised showroom?
Is the completion meter filled by using every slot, or by some scoring of what was placed?
One room only, or does the room open onto more rooms once it is filled?

coverage_missing.ask: Should the room read as a contemporary apartment, a cosy cottage, or a bright stylised showroom?
Is the completion meter filled by using every slot, or by scoring what was placed?
One room only, or does it open onto more rooms once filled?
Room size is stated as a room but not dimensioned - how many placement slots should it hold?

answers.ask: No style is stated beyond real furniture - should the room read as a contemporary apartment, a cosy cottage, or a bright stylised showroom?
answers.answer: Use a contemporary apartment style with a simple, believable furnished-room look.

answers.ask: Is the completion meter filled by using every slot, or by some scoring of what was placed?
answers.answer: Fill the completion meter by placing furniture into every designated placement slot; no additional scoring is needed.

answers.ask: One room only, or does the room open onto more rooms once it is filled?
answers.answer: Build one room only as a complete, playable decorating space.
